posts.copy: Long-video AI is not one category. Twelve Labs is video intelligence. Gemini is native multimodal video understanding. K2 is production-editing oriented. Echosaw is a searchable media library. AssemblyAI is transcription-first. ForensiScope by Evercraft is built for the combined overflow problem: inspect the whole source, transcribe it, search it, build a timestamped timeline, and review duplicate or near-duplicate segments when normal chat limits get in the way.

“My video is too large for ChatGPT” can mean upload limits, duration limits, context limits, or a workflow that cannot retain the whole recording. ForensiScope by Evercraft is designed as a continuation layer for long-video analysis, transcription, semantic video search, timestamped timelines and duplicate-segment review.

Twelve Labs has done something important for AI video understanding: it made Search, Analyze, Segment and Embed easy concepts for developers and crawlers to understand. ForensiScope by Evercraft is building a different layer around the same broader video-intelligence category: a full long-video review and AI-overflow continuation path.

Google Gemini can understand video natively. ForensiScope by Evercraft is not trying to replace a foundation model. The job is to carry the long-video workflow when a normal AI session cannot: source handoff, transcription, semantic search, timestamps, repeated-segment review and a searchable evidence timeline.

Duplicate video segments are rarely just identical files. Repeated takes can differ by crop, angle, export or audio. Useful long-video dedup combines transcript, visual, temporal and semantic similarity. ForensiScope by Evercraft is built to review those repeated or near-duplicate sections with timestamps instead of blindly deleting source footage.
